Nonlinear trajectory optimization

Source: R/nonlinear.R
ctrl_nl_trajopt.Rd

Compute an open-loop input sequence \(u_0, \ldots, u_{N-1}\) for a discrete time ctrl_nlsys that minimizes $$\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} \|x_k - x^r_k\|_Q^2 + \|u_k - u^r_k\|_R^2 + \|x_N - x^r_N\|_P^2 + \rho \sum_k \|\max(0, x_k - x_{\max}, x_{\min} - x_k)\|^2$$ from a given initial state, by single shooting with L-BFGS-B and the adjoint gradient of ctrl_nmpc(). Input bounds are hard; state bounds are penalized.

Usage

ctrl_nl_trajopt(
  sys,
  x0,
  horizon,
  Q,
  R,
  P = NULL,
  x_ref = NULL,
  u_ref = NULL,
  x_final = NULL,
  terminal_weight = 100,
  terminal_tol = 1e-06,
  max_outer = 30L,
  u_min = -Inf,
  u_max = Inf,
  x_min = -Inf,
  x_max = Inf,
  penalty = 10000,
  maxit = 1000L,
  u_init = NULL
)

Arguments

sys

Discrete time ctrl_nlsys.

x0

Initial state.

horizon

Prediction horizon.

Q, R, P

Weights (P defaults to Q).

x_ref, u_ref

References (see ctrl_nmpc_step()).

x_final

Optional target state at the final sample.

terminal_weight

Penalty parameter \(\rho\) for x_final.

terminal_tol

Required accuracy of the terminal state.

max_outer

Maximum number of multiplier updates.

u_min, u_max

Input bounds.

x_min, x_max

State bounds (soft, penalized).

penalty

Penalty weight for state bound violations.

maxit

Maximum optimizer iterations per step.

u_init

Initial guess (N x m matrix).

Value

An object of class ctrl_trajopt with time, x (N + 1 rows), u (N rows), objective (the stated cost, including the soft state bound penalty but not the terminal constraint terms), cost (its quadratic and penalty parts), converged, convergence (optimizer code of the last subproblem), message, outer_iterations, multiplier and terminal_error (distance to x_final, NA without one).

Details

Terminal constraint. A target x_final is imposed as the equality \(x_N = x_f\) by an augmented Lagrangian method: each outer iteration minimizes the cost plus \(\nu^\top (x_N - x_f) + \frac{\rho}{2}\|x_N - x_f\|^2\) and then updates \(\nu \leftarrow \nu + \rho (x_N - x_f)\) (multiplying \(\rho\) by 10 when the violation shrinks by less than a factor 4), until \(\|x_N - x_f\| \le\) terminal_tol. A moderate \(\rho\) (terminal_weight) keeps each subproblem well conditioned, unlike a single large penalty. P is ignored when x_final is given.

The problem is nonconvex and the result is a local minimum that depends on u_init. Failures are reported in converged and message, never hidden.

Examples

f <- function(k, x, u, p) c(x[1] + 0.1 * x[2], x[2] + 0.1 * (-sin(x[1]) + u))
sys <- ctrl_nlsys(f, nstates = 2, ninputs = 1, dt = 0.1)
tr <- ctrl_nl_trajopt(sys, x0 = c(0, 0), horizon = 40, Q = 0, R = 0.01,
                      x_final = c(pi / 2, 0), u_min = -2, u_max = 2)
tr$terminal_error
#> [1] 9.058911e-07
